text:
Hi! I also moved from A2 to B1 while here in Israel, six years ago (I just finished! I got my Israeli citizenship this March 🥳). It is very very important you move in together first and then apply. To apply you will have to submit a number of documents that prove you live together (such as rental contract, but also importantly the bills of the utilities that prove you live together, because it's written that the apartment pays utilities for two people). You will also need to get a number of documents from your country of origin which will take time to collect, and everything needs apostille and notary translation, so I'd suggest you start looking into it. Since your visa expiry date is so soon, really try get an A2 extension through your university so you can stay here while collecting documents and waiting for your appointment.
Do not move to tourist visa! You can't apply for B1 visa from a tourist visa and it has potential to make your life extremely difficult.

It's a pain in the beginning but it becomes less intense and more automatic with time, do not despair! Good luck ❤️
